title: Good Enough to Launch?
focus: 依据证据作出有限上线决定
story:
On Thursday afternoon, the readiness sheet contains one empty box. Priya has tested staff access, the team has checked the limited change process, and the notification tests pass. The afternoon staff still need to practise the fallback.

Elena will not approve the pilot until that box is complete. Daniel does not ask her to overlook it. He asks when the practice can happen and whether we should tell the participating learners that Friday remains provisional.

“Yes,” she says. “They should hear the uncertainty from us.”

The practice finishes later that day. Priya sends a short account of what staff did, including a step that confused them. Noor revises the instruction page, and Priya confirms the wording with the team. We keep the original version in the record so we can see what changed.

Friday's pilot covers two classes at one centre. Participation is optional. Learners who do not want to take part continue through the existing arrangements, and telephone contact remains available to those who need or prefer it. Staff do not assume that sending an email means a learner has received the information.

Our agreement names the people responsible for support. Priya can stop using the new process at the centre. Elena owns the client decision about continuing. Daniel coordinates our response, and I cover the agreed support period from Shanghai. Rui handles a technical check earlier in the day, before his family commitment.

We also record the conditions that stop the pilot: an incorrect class time, repeated notifications, or an inability to maintain the agreed contact record. If one occurs, staff return to the existing process while we establish the facts. A restart requires an explicit agreement; it does not happen because the screen looks normal again.

By the time the centre opens in London, the sky outside our Shanghai office is turning grey. I have a bottle of water, the support number, and an uncomfortable awareness that watching a quiet screen is still work.

The first hour passes without a class-time change. Priya checks that both shifts can find the instructions. I record what we observe and avoid writing successful launch in the notes.

Then a tutor asks to move one of the participating classes to a later time. Priya confirms the arrangement and makes the change. The correct time appears. The agreed email notifications go out once. Staff begin the telephone follow-up for the learners who need it.

Twenty minutes later, Priya calls.

“We've got a handover problem,” she says. “The next receptionist can't tell which calls are complete.”

My stomach tightens. “Has anyone received a second call?”

“One learner has. She was polite, but she asked whether the class had changed again.”

The emails are not repeating. This is different from our internal test failure, but that distinction will not help the learner unless we deal with the confusion. I ask Priya to pause further calls while she checks the records with the two staff members.

They have used separate copies of the paper contact sheet. Both copies contain useful information; neither contains all of it. Our fallback instructions said to keep a contact record. They did not make clear which copy was authoritative during a shift change.

“We need one agreed record before calling anyone else,” I say. “Can the two staff members reconcile their notes together?”

“They can. I'll supervise it.”

I bring Daniel into the call. We record the pause and keep the affected class on the existing process while Priya resolves the handover. Nobody presses a button to make the problem disappear. Three people compare names and notes carefully, and the desk continues its ordinary work around them.

Priya rings us back. With the learner's permission she repeats the question that finally made sense of those two calls: “Is it still the early bus I need, or has the class moved again?” The learner has been standing at the stop with her travel card in her hand. The early bus is due in two minutes. If the class has moved again, she could wait for the next one.

“What did you say?” I ask.

“The class moved once. I read her the time. She read it back. Then she asked me to let her catch her bus.”

We have kept the affected calls paused. At reception the two people on duty now have one sheet between them. Priya asks the outgoing receptionist to show her which names still need calling. The incoming receptionist reads the same names off the same sheet. One of them spots a tick so faint it looks like a fold. They check that entry together and write the result in ink.

Elena comes to the desk. “Are you both happy to work from this copy?” We hear two separate yeses. “Then resume the calls for these two classes. Keep me here for the first one.”

On our screen nothing changes colour. In London somebody picks up a telephone.

At the end of my support period I hand over to the colleague on the rota. Rui has already left to help his family as agreed. His empty seat is a small relief: the plan has held without anyone quietly buying us another hour of his evening.

The review takes place the following week. We have evidence from one real class-time change, not a large sample. We have also learned that an apparently small instruction can affect whether people receive clear information.

Elena agrees to continue the limited pilot with the revised handover procedure. There is no decision to expand to every centre. Telephone calls, the noticeboard, and parts of the old process remain. We schedule another review and identify what evidence it needs.

When someone asks whether the pilot was a success, Daniel looks at the notes.

“It was useful,” he says. “And we have work to do.”

I save that version of the report. Outside, the rain has stopped, and the pavement is bright under the office lights.

phrases.zh: 明确日期尚未最终确定
说明是否参与由当事人选择
建立共同认可的记录来源
说明恢复操作的授权条件

phrases.en: We have evidence from one real change.

practice.grammar: 练习被动语态表达程序要求：A restart must be agreed explicitly. 对比 Elena approves the restart 与 The restart is approved by Elena，说明需要强调责任人时为何不能省略 by 后信息。
practice.pronunciation: 把 We have evidence / from ONE real change / not a large sample 读三遍；突出 one，再用同样节奏说出两个限定证据范围的句子。

questions.q: What is the final readiness check?
questions.a: The afternoon staff must practise the fallback and confirm the revised instructions.

questions.q: What does the learner need to know at the bus stop?
questions.a: Whether the class time has changed again and she still needs the early bus.

questions.q: What does Elena approve after the review?
questions.a: Continuation of the limited pilot with the revised handover procedure, not expansion to every centre.

roleplay.context: 你扮演 Andy，在支持窗口接到 Priya 的电话。保持事实准确并推动下一步。

turns.line: A learner has received a second call.
turns.cue: 确认现象和影响，提出先暂停受影响的电话流程

turns.line: We found two different contact sheets.
turns.cue: 请工作人员共同核对，明确需要单一记录

turns.line: Can we tell everyone the launch was a success?
turns.cue: 限定观察样本，说明问题处理与后续评审

practice.transfer: 用英语做一次九十秒活动试运行汇报：只试过一场、出现签到重复、人工核对恢复。分开说事实、处理、尚不能证明的结论；不要夸大成全面成功。
practice.retell: 不看原文，按准备、启动条件、交接问题、暂停与恢复、评审五步复述。必须说明重复电话和先前内部测试重复邮件不是同一故障。

translations.23-1: 周四下午，准备情况检查表上还剩一个空格。
translations.23-2: Priya已经测试过工作人员的登录权限，团队也检查了限定范围内的修改流程，通知测试同样通过了。
translations.23-3: 下午班的工作人员还需要演练备用流程。
translations.23-4: 这一格没完成，Elena就不会批准试点。
translations.23-6: 他问什么时候能演练，以及是否应该告诉参与的学员，周五仍只是暂定。
translations.23-8: “他们应该由我们来告知这份不确定性。”
translations.23-9: 当天晚些时候，演练完成了。
translations.23-10: Priya发来一份简短记录，说明工作人员做了什么，也写下了一个让他们困惑的步骤。
translations.23-11: Noor修改了那页操作说明，Priya又和团队确认了措辞。
translations.23-12: 我们把原版也留在记录中，方便看出改了什么。
translations.23-13: 周五的试点只涉及一个中心的两节课。
translations.23-15: 不想参加的学员继续沿用现有安排，需要或更愿意通过电话联系的人，仍可以接到电话通知。
translations.23-16: 工作人员不会把邮件发出视为学员已经收到信息。
translations.23-17: 协议明确列出了负责支持的人员。
translations.23-18: Priya有权在中心停止使用新流程。
translations.23-19: Elena负责客户一方关于是否继续的决定。
translations.23-20: Daniel协调我们的响应，我在上海负责约定时段内的支持。
translations.23-21: Rui在当天较早的时候完成技术检查，之后去履行他的家庭安排。
translations.23-22: 我们还记录了叫停试点的条件：课程时间错误、通知重复，或无法维持约定的联系记录。
translations.23-23: 出现其中任何一种情况，工作人员就退回现有流程，同时由我们查明事实。
translations.23-24: 重新启动必须经过明确同意，不能因为界面看起来正常了，就自动继续。
translations.23-25: 伦敦的中心开门时，上海办公室窗外的天色正逐渐暗下来。
translations.23-26: 我备好了一瓶水和支持电话号码，也有些不自在地意识到，守着一个安静的屏幕，同样是在工作。
translations.23-27: 第一个小时过去，没有课程时间发生变化。
translations.23-28: Priya确认了两个班次都能找到操作说明。
translations.23-29: 我记录下观察到的情况，没有在笔记里写“成功上线”。
translations.23-30: 接着，一位老师提出，把参与试点的一节课往后推迟一些。
translations.23-31: Priya确认了安排，并完成修改。
translations.23-32: 正确的时间显示出来了。
translations.23-33: 约定的邮件通知各发送了一次。
translations.23-34: 工作人员开始为需要电话联系的学员进行后续通知。
translations.23-37: “接班的前台看不出哪些电话已经打过了。”
translations.23-41: 她很客气，但问我们是不是课程又改时间了。”
translations.23-43: 这和内部测试中的故障不同，但如果不解决这份困惑，这个区别对学员就没有帮助。
translations.23-44: 我请Priya先暂停继续打电话，和那两位工作人员核对记录。
translations.23-45: 他们分别使用了两份纸质联系表。
translations.23-46: 两份表都有有用的信息，但都不完整。
translations.23-47: 我们的备用流程说明写着要保留联系记录。
translations.23-48: 却没有说明换班时，应以哪一份为准。
translations.23-49: “继续打电话之前，我们得先确定一份大家认可的记录。”我说。
translations.23-50: “能让两位工作人员一起核对笔记吗？”
translations.23-54: 我们记录了这次暂停，在Priya解决交接问题期间，让受影响的课程继续使用现有流程。
translations.23-55: 没有人按一个按钮，就能让问题消失。
translations.23-56: 三个人仔细核对着姓名和记录，前台的日常工作仍在他们身边继续。
translations.23-58: 征得那名学员同意后，她转述了一个问题，我们这才明白两通电话把人弄得有多糊涂：“我还是得赶早一班公交，还是上课时间又改了？”
translations.23-59: 那名学员手里攥着交通卡，一直站在车站等。
translations.23-60: 早一班车还有两分钟就到。
translations.23-61: 要是上课时间又改了，她大可以等下一班。
translations.23-66: 后来她就请我挂电话，说她得赶车了。”
translations.23-67: 这期间，受影响的通知电话一直暂停着。
translations.23-68: 现在前台值班的两个人面前只有一张共用的表。
translations.23-69: Priya请即将交班的前台员工指出，还有哪些人需要电话通知。
translations.23-70: 接班的员工看着同一张表，把那些名字念了一遍。
translations.23-71: 其中一人发现有个勾淡得几乎像道折痕。
translations.23-72: 他们一起核实那一项，用墨水笔写下结果。
translations.23-74: “你们两位都觉得，可以照这份表来吗？”
translations.23-75: 我们听见两个人各答了一声“可以”。
translations.23-76: “那就恢复这两个班的电话通知。
translations.23-77: 第一通我在这儿陪你们打。”
translations.23-78: 我们屏幕上什么都没变色。
translations.23-79: 伦敦那头，有人拿起了电话。
translations.23-80: 我的支持时段结束后，我把工作交给排班表上的下一位同事。
translations.23-81: Rui已经按约定离开，去帮家里人了。
translations.23-82: 看到他的空座位，我反倒松了口气：计划撑住了，谁也没偷偷拿他晚上的一个钟头来填空。
translations.23-84: 我们的证据只来自一次真实的课程时间修改，样本并不大。
translations.23-85: 我们也明白了，一条看似不起眼的说明，可能影响人们收到的信息是否清楚。
translations.23-86: Elena同意采用修改后的交接流程，继续有限范围的试点。
translations.23-87: 我们没有决定扩大到所有中心。
translations.23-88: 电话、公告板，以及部分旧流程仍然保留。
translations.23-89: 我们安排了下一次复盘，并明确需要哪些证据。
translations.23-90: 有人问试点算不算成功，Daniel看了看记录。
translations.23-93: 我保存了这个版本的报告。
translations.23-94: 窗外，雨已经停了，人行道在办公室灯光下泛着光。
